newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel chief warns against Thomson-CSF sale delay.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel chief warns against Thomson-CSF sale delay.

text.p: Alcatel Alsthom chairman Serge Tchuruk warned on Monday against new delays in the privatisation of defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF, saying delays to date have already paralysed defence industry restructuring across Europe.

"The privatisation of Thomson has been lagging for more than a year. If new delays were to occur, this would frankly be bad for the firm," Tchuruk said in an interview to be published in Tuesday's Le Figaro. "But beyond that, the entire restructuring of the European defence industry has been suspended due to France's actions in this matter."
"It is in everyone's interests to respect the calendar. The next government could end up with the privatisation of Thomson among its first major decisions," he said.
Tchuruk had been asked if he feared the French parliamentary election might further delay the planned sale.

Alcatel is one of two French firms, along with Lagardere Groupe, eligible to bid for Thomson-CSF. Firm and final offers for Thomson are due by May 7 and the government hopes to make a decision by the end of June. But the timetable was set down before conservative President Jacques Chirac called a snap parliamentary election for May 25-June 1.
Tchuruk said Alcatel's offer to buy Thomson, which also involves Dassault Aviation and Aerospatiale French restructuring" in the defence industry.
"We would thus be able to resolve a number of problems that have been on our hands for years," he said.
He hoped the winner would be a strong company with a lot of capital, "because that is the main risk.
"A Thomson with worries about its financial base and the continuity of its principal shareholders would be in a fragile position to discuss the future with its European partners," he said.
